title: CLAUDE.md
text: Two layers, bridged .Call: R layer (R/) — user-facing API input validation. Native code assumes inputs already validated, keep checks R. - database.R — hs_database() creates environment-based handle (ptr, scratch, mode, pattern_ids, pattern_flags) S3 class hs_database; hs_compile() fills compiled pointers via .Call. - scan.R / stream.R — hs_scan(), hs_scan_vector(), stream lifecycle. scan entry points share dual return contract: match data frame callback = NULL, callback invocation count (invisibly) callback supplied. Return TRUE callback terminate scanning early. - ext.R — hs_ext() extended-parameter objects; normalize_ext_list() recycles one-per-expression hs_compile(). - serialize.R, constants.R (HS_* flags/modes), errors.R (stop_vectorscan() typed conditions), utils.R (validation helpers, hs_available()). Native layer (src/) — thin C wrapper Vectorscan. - vectorscan.c compiled twice-via HAVE_HS macro: defined, real bindings; without , every entry point stub errors (#ifndef HAVE_HS block top). configure sets -DHAVE_HS. - hs_database_t, hs_scratch_t, hs_stream_t held R external pointers registered C finalizers — free manually R. - init.c registers .Call entry points (prefixed vctrsn_); must stay sync .Call(vctrsn_...) names used R. - link.cpp exists force C++ linker (Vectorscan needs libstdc++).

what: Benchmark 1 — scaling with the number of patterns
title: Benchmarking vectorscan against R's regex engines
text: grow rule set 7 ~1000 time matching phase engine. Vectorscan’s compile cost measured separately ; benchmark times scanning . Compute throughput MB/s columns easy read. see Vectorscan stay roughly flat rules grow, base-R columns degrade roughly linearly n_patterns. whole point compiling N patterns one automaton.
code: n_extra_grid <- c(0L, 25L, 100L, 500L)  scan_one_engine <- function(engine, patterns, text) {   switch(engine,     vectorscan = {       db <- hs_database()       hs_compile(db, expressions = patterns)       time_it(hs_scan(db, text))     },     base_pcre = time_it(       lapply(patterns, function(p) gregexpr(p, text, perl = TRUE))     ),     base_tre = time_it(       lapply(patterns, function(p) gregexpr(p, text))     )   ) }  results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(n_extra_grid, function(n_extra) {   patterns <- make_patterns(n_extra)   data.frame(     n_patterns = length(patterns),     vectorscan = scan_one_engine("vectorscan", patterns, corpus),     base_pcre  = scan_one_engine("base_pcre",  patterns, corpus),     base_tre   = scan_one_engine("base_tre",   patterns, corpus)   ) }))  results #>   n_patterns vectorscan base_pcre base_tre #> 1          7      0.002     0.009    0.023 #> 2         32      0.002     0.010    0.074 #> 3        107      0.002     0.012    0.223 #> 4        507      0.002     0.015    1.024 mb <- nchar(corpus) / 1024 / 1024 throughput <- data.frame(   n_patterns = results$n_patterns,   vectorscan_mb_s = round(mb / results$vectorscan, 1),   base_pcre_mb_s  = round(mb / results$base_pcre,  1),   base_tre_mb_s   = round(mb / results$base_tre,   1) ) throughput #>   n_patterns vectorscan_mb_s base_pcre_mb_s base_tre_mb_s #> 1          7            85.8           19.1           7.5 #> 2         32            85.8           17.2           2.3 #> 3        107            85.8           14.3           0.8 #> 4        507            85.8           11.4           0.2

what: Benchmark 4 — callback vs. data frame collection
title: Benchmarking vectorscan against R's regex engines
text: hs_scan() supports two output modes: collect every match data frame (default), invoke R callback per match. Intuitively callback sounds cheaper avoids building data frame, invocation crosses C → R boundary pays interpreter cost per event. Let’s measure. corpus data-frame path dramatically faster — match collection happens entirely C, callback path pays C → R round-trip per match event. callback still right tool : want early termination (return TRUE stop scanning). match set enormous need fold (counts, sketches, sampling) without ever materializing . want stream matches another system arrive. everything else — including “just count ” — let data frame form call nrow().
code: patterns <- make_patterns(50L) db <- hs_database() hs_compile(db, expressions = patterns)  cb_time <- time_it({   ctx <- new.env()   ctx$n <- 0L   hs_scan(db, corpus,     callback = function(id, from, to, flags, context) {       context$n <- context$n + 1L       FALSE     },     context = ctx   ) }, n = 5L)  df_time <- time_it(hs_scan(db, corpus), n = 5L)  data.frame(   mode = c("callback (counts only)", "data frame (collects all)"),   seconds = round(c(cb_time, df_time), 4) ) #>                        mode seconds #> 1    callback (counts only)   0.121 #> 2 data frame (collects all)   0.002

title: Getting started with vectorscan
text: Vectored mode treats list buffers one logical input. Streaming mode keeps scan state across arbitrarily many chunks, useful input arrives time large hold memory. Always close stream done; close step also reports pending matches.
code: db <- hs_database(HS_MODE_VECTORED) hs_compile(db, "foobar") hs_scan_vector(db, c("foo", "bar")) #>   id from to flags #> 1  0   NA  6     0 db <- hs_database(HS_MODE_STREAM) hs_compile(db, "foo.*bar")  stream <- hs_stream_open(db) hs_stream_scan(stream, "foo") #> [1] id    from  to    flags #> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names) hs_stream_scan(stream, " and then bar") #>   id from to flags #> 1  0   NA 16     0 hs_stream_close(stream) #> [1] id    from  to    flags #> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

code: db <- hs_database() hs_compile(db, "foo")  path <- tempfile(fileext = ".hsdb") hs_save(db, path)  restored <- hs_load(path) hs_scan(restored, "foo") #>   id from to flags #> 1  0   NA  3     0

title: R Bindings to Vectorscan and Hyperscan
text: hs_* scanning functions map one one onto Vectorscan API: compile database chosen mode, scan single blocks, vectored blocks streams, flags extended parameters Vectorscan offers. Use callback handle matches reported Vectorscan. Return TRUE callback terminate scanning early. Vectored mode scans adjacent buffers one logical input: Streaming mode keeps scan state across chunks: Compiled databases can serialized:
code: db <- hs_database(mode = HS_MODE_BLOCK) hs_compile(   db,   expressions = c("foo", "^foobar$", "BAR"),   ids = c(0L, 1L, 2L),   flags = c(     HS_FLAG_NONE,     HS_FLAG_NONE,     bitwOr(HS_FLAG_CASELESS, HS_FLAG_SOM_LEFTMOST)   ) )  hs_scan(db, "foobar") #>   id from to flags #> 1  0   NA  3     0 #> 2  2    3  6     0 #> 3  1   NA  6     0 hs_scan(   db,   "foobar",   callback = function(id, from, to, flags, context) {     print(list(id = id, from = from, to = to, source = context$source))     FALSE   },   context = list(source = "example") ) db <- hs_database(HS_MODE_VECTORED) hs_compile(db, "foobar") hs_scan_vector(db, c("foo", "bar")) db <- hs_database(HS_MODE_STREAM) hs_compile(db, "foo.*bar")  stream <- hs_stream_open(db) hs_stream_scan(stream, "foo") hs_stream_scan(stream, " and then bar") hs_stream_close(stream) db <- hs_database() hs_compile(db, "foo")  bytes <- hs_serialize(db) restored <- hs_deserialize(bytes) hs_scan(restored, "foo")

title: vectorscan — Roadmap
text: Strengths Complete low-level binding core Hyperscan API: block / vectored / streaming scans, callbacks early termination, extended parameters, serialization, database metadata. Self-contained build: vendored Vectorscan 5.4.13 (~8.1 MB, 682 files) compiled private static libhs install time, system-lib stub fallbacks development. Good engineering hygiene age: typed error conditions, external pointers C finalizers, roxygen docs, pkgdown config, two vignettes — including honest benchmark vignette shows Vectorscan win. Gaps API C-shaped, R-shaped. hs_scan() takes one string returns byte offsets. dominant R idiom — “match patterns character vector, give back elements matched text” — expressible without manual loop R. matched-text extraction; users get offsets must slice bytes (offsets byte offsets, undocumented UTF-8). Thin test suite (~130 lines) coverage serialization round-trips, stream edge cases, UTF-8, large inputs, error paths native code, callback misbehavior (errors thrown inside callbacks). CI (since 2026-09-26) checks bundled build Linux, macOS Windows, CRAN-like containers, ASan, UBSan, valgrind, LTO, gctorture rchk. system-library stub build modes exercised yet. CRAN. Ragel Boost longer build requirements source tarball 1.25 MB; build time main remaining risk (see Stage 4). Positioning: package deserves exist R’s regex options — TRE/PCRE (base), ICU (stringi/stringr), RE2 (re2), Oniguruma (ore) — match one pattern per pass. AhoCorasickTrie multi-pattern matching literals . Nothing ecosystem compiles thousands regexes single automaton walks input . Vectorscan’s structural advantage, maps concrete R user pain: Security / log analytics: secret & PII scanning, IOC matching, SIEM rule sets log corpora (benchmark vignette already leans way). Data cleaning scale: “flag every row matching 5,000 patterns” — today O(patterns × rows) grepl() loop. Bioinformatics / text mining: motif dictionary scanning large sequences corpora, streaming files big memory. strategy one sentence: keep faithful low-level hs_* layer, win adoption vectorized, stringr-flavored high-level layer top — make package installable everywhere (CRAN) prove performance story reproducible benchmarks.

Callback errors caught R_tryEval() re-raised scan, longjmp crosses Vectorscan; ASan job exercises path. - serialization: round-trip equivalence, hs_save()/hs_load(), corrupt-bytes error path, cross-mode deserialization. - streams: matches spanning chunk boundaries, matches reported hs_stream_close(), scanning closed stream, stream outliving database (GC/finalizer ordering). - callbacks: R error thrown inside callback mid-scan (longjmp C frame — verify leak/corruption; unsafe, fix Stage 2 R_UnwindProtect). - inputs: empty strings, embedded NULs via raw vectors, non-ASCII UTF-8, large inputs, hs_ext() parameters actually affecting matches. - validation: one test per stop_vectorscan() class. what: Stage 2 — The R-native API: make it feel like R
title: vectorscan — Roadmap
text: Goal: R user knows stringr productive five minutes. stage adoption driver — prioritize everything except safety. Vectorized scanning (centerpiece) hs_match(db, x) — scan character vector, return tidy data frame: input (element index), id/pattern, , , match (extracted text). Implemented C: loop elements reusing one scratch, per-element R overhead. hs_detect(db, x) — grepl() scale: logical vector (“pattern hit?”) plus variant returning per-pattern results (element × pattern logical matrix list-column). hs_count(db, x) — match counts per element (respecting HS_FLAG_SINGLEMATCH semantics set). hs_extract(db, x) — matched substrings; auto-enable HS_FLAG_SOM_LEFTMOST needed (documented opt-, since SOM costs compile-time/state). Done 2026-09-26: four verbs scan C (vctrsn_hs_scan_many, one scratch per call); hs_detect() stops element first match. hs_extract() returns list per element, like stringr::str_extract_all(). Matched text sliced R, next thing move C profiling says (Stage 3). Ergonomics Named patterns: accept named character vector data frame rules (pattern, id, flags, ext columns) hs_compile(); carry names match output. real rule sets (secret scanners, IOC feeds) arrive. One-call convenience: hs_compile() bare character vector without pre-creating database (hs_database() becomes optional plumbing). Literal API: bind hs_compile_lit_multi() massive literal dictionaries (regex escaping footguns, faster compiles). Encoding correctness: document byte vs character offsets; provide character-offset conversion UTF-8 inputs (return ). Callback safety: wrap callback invocation R_UnwindProtect error inside R callback leak scratch/stream state. Flag ergonomics: accept flag names strings (flags = c("caseless", "som_leftmost")) alongside integer constants. Richer print.hs_database: pattern count, mode, database size. Deliverable docs Rewrite “Getting started” vignette around vectorized verbs; relegate low-level hs_* C-shaped API “low-level interface” section/vignette. Exit criteria: user can replace grepl(paste(pats, collapse="|"), x) two lines vectorscan get pattern-level attribution, matched text, 10–100× speedup large pattern sets.

title: vectorscan — Roadmap
text: Goal: turn text columns one regex, least 10× faster utils::strcapture(). motivating case reading log file data frame (timestamp, level, location, text). M0 (done 2026-09-26) measured base R’s time goes. 1M log lines, strcapture() takes 12.5 s, PCRE2 matches lines 0.23 s: rest building R objects. C loop PCRE2 JIT writes columns directly takes 0.13 s. Chimera 7.5× slower every line matches, hs_capture() runs PCRE2 directly (preferably one R uses), Vectorscan prefilter rule sets. Plan numbers: .agents/capture-groups.md. M0 Benchmark gate: base R, PCRE2 + JIT Chimera 1M lines (tools/bench-capture/). M1 PCRE2 build: system PCRE2 (Rtools, pkg-config) vendored 10.48 fallback hidden symbols; build-modes job symbol-collision setting. M2 C capture loop: columns filled place; differential test regexec(perl = TRUE); sanitizers clean. M3 R API: hs_capture(pattern, x, proto) like strcapture(), least 10× faster; docs, “Parsing logs” article, benchmarks. M4 Vectorscan prefilter rule sets: route lines formats hs_match(), capture PCRE2. M5 Hardening: match depth limits, invalid UTF-8, JIT fallback. Exit criteria: hs_capture() platforms, sanitizer-clean, identical strcapture() tests least 10× faster.

title: vectorscan — Roadmap
text: Goal: “fast” claim receipts, handle data doesn’t fit memory. Scratch management parallelism: expose hs_scratch_clone() semantics databases can shared across threads/processes; document (test) one-scratch-per-thread rule. Parallel vectorized scan: optional OpenMP (thread pool) elements hs_match()/hs_detect() — Vectorscan scans callback-driven C, true parallelism feasible R callback involved. File/connection streaming helpers: hs_scan_file(db, path, chunk_size) built streaming API — scan multi-GB logs without loading ; line-number attribution matches. Database caching: pattern-set hashing + hs_serialize() skip recompilation large rule sets across sessions (compiles 10k+ patterns expensive). Benchmark vignette v2: add stringi re2 (just base R), scaling curves (patterns × corpus size), compile-time vs scan-time breakdown, memory footprint; publish results pkgdown site. Micro-optimizations informed profiling: match-buffer growth policy, avoiding enc2utf8() copies already-UTF-8 vectors, ALTREP-aware string access. Exit criteria: published, reproducible benchmarks showing crossover points vs base R / stringi / re2; multi-GB file scanning works bounded memory.

title: vectorscan — Roadmap
text: Goal: install.packages("vectorscan") works everywhere R runs. hardest stage; start de-risking early. Known blockers mitigations: Ragel: present CRAN build machines. Pre-generate ragel outputs (.rl → .cpp) vendor generated sources, dropping ragel SystemRequirements entirely. Boost headers: avoid requiring system Boost. Options, order preference: () point CMake build BH package’s headers via LinkingTo: BH + BOOST_ROOT; (b) vendor small subset Boost headers Vectorscan actually uses. Tarball size: 1.25 MB compressed (773 files) Vectorscan 5.4.13, measured 2026-09-26 – well ceiling, pruning needed. Original item: measure compressed source tarball; prune vendored tree (per-arch SIMD sources platforms CRAN doesn’t ship, cmake scaffolding). CRAN’s informal ceiling ~5 MB — request exception justification pruning can’t get . Build time: CRAN checks time ; tune bundled build (single target, -j2, FAT_RUNTIME=baseline SIMD) measure slowest platform. Measured CI 2026-09-26: single install x86-64 fat runtime -j2 takes 5 min; full R CMD check (two builds, -j4) 8 min macOS, 11-17 min Linux 20 min Windows. Windows Intel macOS already build without fat runtime. Architecture coverage: verify builds CRAN’s actual fleet — x86-64 Linux/Windows (ucrt), macOS x86-64 + arm64 (NEON path). CI covers x86-64 Linux Windows arm64 macOS; Intel macOS exercised. Also decide behavior unsupported arches (fail install vs stub build — CRAN accept package whose examples/tests skip, unsupported-arch policy must explicit). Interim channel: publish r-universe now (pedrobtz.r-universe.dev) binary installs continuous checks CRAN feasible. CRAN submission checklist: cran-comments.md, win-builder + mac-builder runs, rhub2 sweep, Additional_repositories/SystemRequirements accuracy, reverse-dependency-free first release. Vendored-source upgrade policy: tools/vendor/ (manifest pinned commit sha256, keep list, patches tools/patches/, verify), vendor guard vendor-upstream release watcher; updated 5.4.13. Original item: Define vendored-source upgrade policy: script sync upstream (tools/update-vendor.sh), record upstream commit, track Vectorscan releases (5.4.x → current) CVEs. Exit criteria: CRAN (documented, dated plan remaining blockers), r-universe binaries available meanwhile.

title: vectorscan — Roadmap
text: Goal: obvious answer someone asks “match 10,000 patterns fast R?” Use-case vignettes / pkgdown articles, targeting searchable problem: - “Scanning logs secrets PII” (expand benchmark vignette’s rule set worked example). - “Matching IOC / threat-intel feeds network logs.” - “Dictionary motif scanning text mining / bioinformatics.” Interop sugar: examples (hard dependencies) data.table, dplyr/tidyr list-column workflows, arrow/duckdb pipelines feeding hs_scan_file(). Evaluate Chimera add-(Hyperscan’s PCRE hybrid): measured 2026-09-26 chosen. PCRE2 JIT 7.5× faster capture groups every line matches (Stage 2b). Revisit Vectorscan 5.5 moves Chimera PCRE2. Community scaffolding: CONTRIBUTING.md, issue templates, NEWS.md discipline per release, lifecycle badges. Announce: r-universe listing, R Weekly submission, blog post built around benchmark story, rOpenSci soft-review consideration. Track adoption: CRAN downloads, GitHub issues theme — feed back roadmap re-prioritization. Exit criteria: organic issues/questions arriving real users; package appears search results target problems.

title: vectorscan — Roadmap
text: Stages 1 → 2 strictly ordered: don’t build high-level API untested native layer. Stage 4’s de-risking spikes (ragel pre-generation, BH headers, tarball size measurement) start Stage 2 — CRAN turns impossible current shape, changes vendoring decisions early. single highest-leverage item whole plan hs_match() / hs_detect() character vectors (Stage 2). Without package niche C binding; , answers question thousands R users actually .

title: vectorscan 0.0.0.9000
text: New hs_capture() turns text data frame one regular expression: one row per element, one column per capture group, named named groups typed proto utils::strcapture(). returns data frame strcapture(perl = TRUE) 20-27 times faster million log lines, matching PCRE2 (JIT) filling columns C. hs_capture_compile() compiles pattern reuse. See “Parsing logs” article. PCRE2 now part build, upcoming hs_capture(): system PCRE2 (>= 10.34) available, else bundled PCRE2 10.48 compiled symbols hidden clash PCRE2 R loads. VECTORSCAN_PCRE2 selects route. New vectorized verbs scan whole character vector one call: hs_detect() (like grepl() many patterns), hs_count(), hs_match() (data frame every match pattern, offsets text) hs_extract(). take compiled block-mode database patterns ; given patterns, hs_match() hs_extract() turn start--match offsets automatically. hs_compile() accepts named patterns rules data frames (pattern, id, flags, name), hs_compile(patterns) without database returns new block-mode database. Initial package implementation native bindings compiling databases, block scanning, vectored scanning, streaming, database metadata, database serialization. package now vendors Vectorscan source builds native library source default configuration. bundled Vectorscan updated 5.4.13, fixes stack buffer overflow rvermicelliDoubleExecReal(), AVX-512 scanning bug, SVE accelerator bugs, integer overflow, wrong page-size assumption Apple Silicon, compiler errors clang 21 GCC 15/16. Invalid character classes now compile error. Compile errors now report Vectorscan’s message correctly; read freed. hs_deserialize() hs_load() now restore database mode per-pattern flags, restored database reports matches exactly like original (stays NA patterns compiled without HS_FLAG_SOM_LEFTMOST; used come back 0). hs_serialize() still returns plain Vectorscan bytes, pattern ids flags attached attributes. hs_save() now writes small tagged header (VSCANRDB) metadata bytes; hs_load() reads format plain Vectorscan files. VECTORSCAN_USE_SYSTEM=true without system libhs now fails configure, bundled build , instead silently building runtime stubs; set VECTORSCAN_ALLOW_STUBS=true get stubs. Fixed read past end input bundled Vectorscan (vermicelliExec), hit scan ends inside run repeated character, example foo.*bar chunk xs streaming mode. crash R input ended page boundary. Windows Intel macOS bundled library now built x86-64-v2 (SSE4.2); x86-64 Linux keeps per-CPU dispatch. Linux distributions install libraries lib64 (Fedora, RHEL, openSUSE) now build correctly.
